Holds 105 object records. Setup at $3765 reads column, row, type and flags. The row and column choose where the tile patch begins when flag $20 is set.
The first $FF in the column field ends LEVELC's object list at $3773. The final record is four bytes of $FF.

Initialize the viewport row to $86 in $46 and its column to $15 in $45. Store the row plus $0A in $E690 and the column plus $14 in $E630. Clear $1D, $1F and $390C, then seed $CA35 with $03 and return with carry set.
Return immediately from the actor callback. The corresponding descriptor slot passes control through $15EB and this RTS returns to the engine.
Set the border colour to zero and continue to the playfield glyph update at $C86D.
The 15 pointers index LEVELC's rectangular tile patches. $37B1 reads the low byte and $37B6 reads the next byte for the high byte.

Initialize LEVELC actor type $2D in slot X. Store $0A in horizontal extent. Store $13 in vertical extent. Store $02 in $E9F0, $EA80. Store $08 in horizontal movement. Set $EB10 to $80 to select direct sprite shapes. Store $0C in sprite colour.

Initialize LEVELC actor type $2F in slot X. Store $0B in horizontal extent. Store $13 in vertical extent. Store $01 in $E9F0, $EA80. Store $10 in horizontal movement. Store $14 in $E840. Store $04 in sprite colour.
Initialize LEVELC actor type $30 in slot X. Store $0B in horizontal extent. Store $13 in vertical extent. Store $02 in $E9F0, $EA80. Store $0E in sprite colour.
Set $E840 to sixteen plus the low five random bits. Set colour four, clear both movement fields, set the extents to twelve and eighteen and set $E9F0 and $EA80 to two and zero.
Set extents to ten and eighteen, $E9F0 and $EA80 to three, colour five, actor flag $04 and $E870 to $0F.
Write fourteen to the actor's sprite colour field.
Set colour fourteen, both extents to eighteen, $E9F0 to zero and $E840 to four. Choose whether to clear or set direction bit $08 from the random byte at $1A57.
Clear visibility bit $40 in the current slot's flags.
Set $EA50 to $FF, $E9F0 to four, $EA80 to six and the two extents to eight and eleven, then jump to $C59F.
Set $EA50 to $FF and copy the low three actor flag bits to $E840 if any are set. Clear the copied bits from the flags.
Set horizontal extent two and vertical extent three, then use the common flag transfer at $C47B.
Set horizontal extent four and vertical extent two, then use the common flag transfer at $C47B.

Set $E9F0 and $EA80 to three and two and extents to ten and eighteen. Set $E870 to four plus the low three random bits. Set colour five, actor flag $04 and direct shape $AC, and clear $E9C0 and $E750.
Initialize LEVELC actor type $37 in slot X. Store $08 in horizontal extent, $E9F0, $EA80. Store $04 in vertical extent. Store $0E in sprite colour. Apply $04 with OR to actor flags.
Initialize LEVELC actor type $35 in slot X. Store $FF in $EA50. Store $08 in sprite colour. Store $12 in horizontal extent, vertical extent.
An immediate return between the colour-eight initializer and the timed actor initializer.

Initialize LEVELC actor types $2A, $2B in slot X. Store $01 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Apply $34 with OR to actor flags. Apply $01 with OR to shape and actor flags at $EB10. Store $FF in $EA50. Store $0F in $E870.
Initialize LEVELC actor type $31 in slot X. Store $02 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Store $FF in $EA50.
Set extents to $18 and $28, clear $E9F0, $EA80, $1D, $1F and $E9C0, then call $C57A. Allocate type $27 at this actor's coordinates and save the parent slot in the child at $E900.
Initialize LEVELC actor type $27 in slot X. Store $04 in sprite colour. Store $FF in $EA50. Apply $10 with OR to actor flags. Set $EB10 to $80 to select direct sprite shapes.
Set actor flag $10 and coarse row three. The remaining instructions clear the visibility flag.
Clear actor flag $40 and return after the field changes made by the calling initializer.
Initialize LEVELC actor type $28 in slot X. Apply $20 with OR to actor flags.
Set horizontal movement to $10. Test $275A, $E840 and $2760 before taking the random branch that calls $28AF with $2A stored in $08. Then pass four in $08 to the turn routine at $1B64.

Select shape zero or two from the direction bit and call $2742, then test $275A. If that returns carry clear, call $2838 when $E840 equals $E870 and count $E840 down. At zero use the turn check after $1B64 and set horizontal movement to $10.
Call $279E with two. If carry is set, pass five to $2760 and return its carry.
Call $2742 with eight and decrement $E870. On underflow reload it to $14 and ask $2760 whether to spawn four actors through $C823.
Clear actor flag $04. Call $2757 with four and pass eight in $08 to the turn logic at $1B75. At the end reload $1A57 and test its low three bits. Both outcomes return.
Call $2742 with eight, then use the patrol path at $C731.

Call $275A with four and subtract four from vertical movement. Select shape $A4 or, when the signed branch at $C676 succeeds, set shape $A5 and movement five and $28. The branch calls $2927 and counts down $E840. At zero reinitialize the slot as type $37 and reload $E840 to four.
Run $275A and select the shape from $E960 shifted right once. On timer underflow reload $E840 with $46 and reuse the spawn test at $C635.

Clear horizontal movement and run $275A and the shape cycle at $C6FC. When that cycle reaches phase zero, decrement $E840. On underflow set horizontal movement to $20 and reset the timer to two. Inspect and set flag $04 and decrement $E870, using $C6F6 when the reset is selected.
Call $2927 and restart initialization at $C4AD.

Decrement $E750 and return when it is nonnegative. Reload it to five on underflow, decrement $E9C0 and use incoming A if its new value is negative. Use the direction bit to choose the frame group and copy the indexed pointer to $E7E0.
Four shape pointers for the direction with actor flag $08 set, indexed by $E9C0.
The other direction's four shape pointers, indexed by the same phase byte.
The shared Stage 3 patrol update enters $C5B1 through this jump.

On carry from $22E5 advance the actor one coarse row and call $381A. A zero $E840 removes it. A value of one subtracts nine rows and changes the type to $25 through $3854. Other nonzero values instead change it to type $2D and use $C370, clearing flag $20. The path at $C786 compares player proximity and selects the argument to $27DA from relative coarse X.
A second return between the end of the converting actor's update and the type $2D animation entry.
Run $275A and the turn logic. When $E750 reaches zero, reset it to five and select the shape at $C7D9 using the four-phase counter and the group offset selected by direction.
Two groups of four shape pointers, selected by the phase and direction at $C7A8.

Run $275A and decrement $E840. On underflow reload it to $14 and flip direction. A successful $2760 test spawns the group at $C823. When $E750 reaches zero reload it to five and alternate the low shape bit, choosing the pair by the direction flag.
Call $C84C for each of four shots. Give the first two opposite vertical movements and the latter two horizontal magnitude $40, toggling the last one's direction.
Allocate type $2B, set its $E870 timer to ten and copy the parent position using $22CC.
Decrement $E870 and remove the actor when it turns negative. Otherwise call the resident check at $287A.
Call $287A only when the playfield glyph animation phase is zero.

Decrement the timer at $C8FC. When it underflows, reload $0A and advance the phase at $C8FD modulo four. Copy 32 bytes backwards into $79C0–$79DF, replacing glyphs $38–$3B in the playfield character set.
The four phase offsets $1F, $3F, $5F and $3F point to the last byte of each 32-byte animation frame relative to $C89C. The copying loop counts down from the selected end.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 0. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $38–$3B.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 1 and 3. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $38–$3B.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 2. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $38–$3B.
Countdown in calls to the stage update. Underflow reloads it with $0A and advances the animation phase.
The update increments this value modulo four and uses it to index the backwards-copy offsets at $C898.

Call $38BD and return when $390C is set. Use $23B7 to choose colour four or one. On carry from $275A, decrement $CA35 if nonzero. When it is zero, set $390C to $14, restore type $26, clear visibility and call $38BD. Otherwise count the shape timer down and use the lower counter to select a shape and periodically spawn four shots.

Copy the parent's X, add $0250 to its two-byte Y and copy its colour. Select the shape from $C9CD using the parent's $E840. Remove this actor if $390C is set, the parent is no longer type $26, or its flags are zero or have bit zero set.
Jump past the final parent-flag checks to the shared return at $C9BA.
Read the parent's flags in slot Y. Go to $2739 to flag the follower for removal when those flags are zero or bit zero is set.
Direct sprite pointers indexed by the parent timer $E840 at $C95B.
Direct sprite pointers indexed by the parent's $E840 in the follower at $C963.
When $1F is set increment the colour and set visibility flag $40. Test each active player unless $1D is negative. Carry from $23D6 calls $216F and then marks the actor for removal.
Stage 3 type $28 immediately returns from this update callback.

If $1D is nonzero, store its low seven bits at $70 and set $1E to three. Allocate type $28 at the actor's coordinates and mark the old slot for removal. Pass the new slot to $3854 and request map refresh through $4F.
The parent update tests this byte and counts it down on the carry-set path from $275A. Reaching zero sets $390C, restores type $26 and clears visibility.
